decision.question: review size
decision.why: pure move of Columns and Links out of Page.class.js behind same-named facades; old-vs-new browser parity probes at 4 widths were identical, smoke clean

findings.text: `Columns.js:176-179,193` — the internal calls (`settle`→`even`/`scroll`, the ResizeObserver) go straight to `PageColumns` methods instead of back through `page.settle_columns`/`page.even_columns`, while the header comment says every call goes through `this.page.*`. No page overrides these today (grep of `public/` finds none), so nothing breaks; only an override of those facades would be bypassed.

`Page.class.js` facades build a fresh `new this.constructor.Columns({page: this})` on every call, including the per-frame/resize `settle_columns` and `scroll_column`. It is cheap (one tiny object), but one cached instance per page would be simpler if it ever shows in a profile.

`Links.js:11` — `open`/`swap` now call `PageLinks.md_file`/`md_url` rather than `Page.md_file`, so a subclass that overrides the static `Page.md_file` would no longer affect `open_link`. No such override exists in the diff; it is a small behaviour change from the old `Page.md_*` calls.

`STATE.md` records measurements for step 5 as n/a (only line count), so the "before/after in STATE.md" ask is met in full only for step 6. The line counts (1315 → 1173 → 1086) are enough to see the shrink.

Both asks are met: Columns and Links are separate class files, `columns()`, `column()`, `column_host`, `open_link`, `swap_link` keep their signatures as facades, `split-plan.md` is ticked, and the old-vs-new browser comparison at the four widths is in `STATE.md`. I did not re-run the pages; the pass rests on the diff and STATE.md.
